title: Stability corridor: regression probes and auto-rollback policy for eval prompt suites
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a ‘stability corridor’ mechanism that continuously probes candidate model variants against a curated eval prompt suite and triggers deterministic auto-rollback when quality or safety metrics cross configurable thresholds. The feature should integrate with canary and A/B pipelines and support both shadow traffic and live canary traffic.

Motivation: Current rollouts rely on infrequent evaluations and manual checks. We need a lightweight, production-safe probe loop that provides early detection of regressions tied to concrete prompt sets (customer golden prompts, privacy-safe synthetic probes, and representative sampling). The system must minimize false positives, be explainable to PMs/SEs, and fit within existing rollout orchestration.

Scope:
- Probe runner service that executes eval prompt suites at a configurable cadence (per-candidate window).
- Scorecard computation: per-prompt metrics (token-level loss proxies, logprob deltas, semantic similarity via embeddings, safety flag counts) and aggregate signals (median delta, top-5 regressions).
- Adaptive thresholds: baseline-relative thresholds that scale with prompt variance, and an optional strict mode for high-risk customers.
- Decision policy: deterministic rollback if any of the following hold for N consecutive windows: (1) critical-safety count increase >X; (2) median quality delta worse than -Y%; (3) top-k prompt regressions exceed M prompts.
- Integration points: rollout controller (canary flip), console dashboard (per-rollout probe timeline), alerting (PagerDuty + Slack), audit log entries, and customer-level overrides.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Probe runner runs scheduled evals for canaries and stores per-prompt results in the eval database.
2) Scorecards are visible in console per release and per customer, with drift plots.
3) Auto-rollback triggers for staged policy in our QA environment and a dry-run mode can be enabled for production rollouts.
4) False positive rate on internal canary experiments <3% over 30 days.

Non-goals: automated model retraining, full human-in-the-loop review engine, or replacing long-form human evals.

2025-02-18 - Liam Chen: Spike complete — implemented probe runner prototype that replays 200 prompts against candidate and baseline; collected token loss deltas. Results in /dashboards/probes/spike-20250218.

2025-02-25 - Security (Ethan Roy): Confirmed encryption-at-rest for eval artifacts and recommended KMS tagging; flagged that customer prompts containing PII must only be used in private deployments. Marked security_review_required=true.

2025-03-01 - Liam Chen: Implemented aggregation functions (median delta, top-K regression rank). Added baseline-relative adaptive thresholds; pushed initial PR for probe runner: github.com/redwood-inference/probes/pull/187.
2025-03-03 - PM sync (Aisha): Decided to ship dry-run auto-rollback in runtime-1.21 canaries for internal teams only; production enablement gated behind 2-week stable window and SRE signoff.

2025-03-05 - QA (Sana Ibrahim): Ran extended simulation across 12 model pairs; observed 2.4% false positives at current thresholds. Proposed relaxing top-K threshold from 5 -> 7 for median-sensitive suites. Next: tune thresholds and add canary-level overrides.
